text: The impresario had fixed forty days. <break time="0.8s" /> As the longest period of fasting. <break time="0.8s" /> Beyond which he would never allow it to continue. <break time="0.8s" /> Not even in the great cities. <break time="0.8s" /> And he had good reason for this limit. <break time="0.8s" /> Experience had shown. <break time="0.8s" /> That for about forty days. <break time="0.8s" /> The publics interest could be stirred up. <break time="0.8s" /> By steadily increasing advertising. <break time="0.8s" /> But after that it began to fade. <break time="0.8s" /> And a clear decline in attendance. <break time="0.8s" /> Could be observed. <break time="0.8s" /> So on the fortieth day. <break time="0.8s" /> The door of the flower decked cage was opened. <break time="0.8s" /> A military band played. <break time="0.8s" /> And two doctors entered the cage. <break time="0.8s" /> To take the necessary measurements. <break time="0.8s" /> The results of which were announced. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a megaphone. <break time="0.8s" /> Then two young ladies. <break time="0.8s" /> Delighted to have been chosen for the honor. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to lead him out of the cage. <break time="0.8s" /> And down a few steps. <break time="0.8s" /> To a small table. <break time="0.8s" /> On which a light meal for invalids was waiting. <break time="0.8s" /> At this moment, however. <break time="0.8s" /> The hunger artist always resisted. <break time="0.8s" /> And although he willingly laid his bony arms. <break time="0.8s" /> In the ladies helpful hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He refused to stand up. <break time="0.8s" /> Asking himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Why he should stop now, after only forty days. <break time="0.8s" /> He could have held out longer. <break time="0.8s" /> So why should he be robbed of the glory. <break time="0.8s" /> Of not merely being the greatest hunger artist of all time. <break time="0.8s" /> A title he had perhaps already earned. <break time="0.8s" /> But of surpassing even himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the impresario stepped forward. <break time="0.8s" /> And lifted his arms over the artist. <break time="0.8s" /> As though inviting heaven itself. <break time="0.8s" /> To admire this pitiful martyr on the straw. <break time="0.8s" /> And a martyr he truly was though in an entirely different sense. <break time="0.8s" /> Gripping the frail waist. <break time="0.8s" /> With exaggerated care. <break time="0.8s" /> He handed the artist over to the pale ladies. <break time="0.8s" /> And while a meal was fed. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the half fainting man. <break time="0.8s" /> The impresario chatted cheerfully. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep the audience from noticing his condition.
